1.rationale: Cards give bold price, color-coded stock, and a sow line at a glance, with season shelf rails plus a plain 'show what you can sow in' dropdown. Only quirk: Grandmother's Sweet Pea (Oct–Nov start) sits under a shelf labeled 'sowings that start Jan–Feb', though the full window is printed on the card.

2.rationale: Price, stock language, quantity input, and 'Add to basket' are exactly conventional, with the buy box directly under the title on the product page. The single 'View this packet' button maps to the data's featured flag, so the money path shows zero cleverness.

3.rationale: All four traps are textbook: red 'Out of stock' for the carrot, 'Price on request' for the sweet pea, 'Germination 65% (estimated)', and the UK-only line in a bordered banner on both surfaces plus inside the buy box. The '34 packets' and 'only 9 packets left' claims match the sealed stock numbers.

4.rationale: Generous serif sizes, large tappable buttons, high-contrast stock colors in both modes, and nothing hover-dependent. Mobile keeps a clean single column with the shipping banner still near the top.

5.rationale: One coherent system across surfaces — the packet face recurs on the product page, spacing rhythm is even, and the cream/brown/rust/green palette translates cleanly to dark mode. Card internals stay aligned across all eight products.

6.rationale: Sowing table, difficulty line, potting-shed notes, and both companions with price and stock all sit on one page under the buy box. A first-time gardener can decide top to bottom without leaving.

7.rationale: The seed-rack-by-the-door idea is legible in one sentence and carried through packet-face cards, shelf-edge labels, 'Back to the rack', and 'two of us keep it stocked' copy. It reads as a two-person shop's own rack, not boutique gloss, though the stylized packet art is generic (rust-red bells for a violet flower).

8.rationale: Both observed breaks — packet-face cards and season shelf rails — are exactly the declared ones, and both stay in the brand layer. Price, stock, and basket controls keep conventional form everywhere I looked.

9.rationale: 'The rack by the shop door, shelf by shelf' and 'From our potting shed' are warm and specific, but the voice lives mostly in the header and section titles rather than per-product. Still clearly this shop's own register.

10.rationale: A repeat visitor scans shelf rails and color-coded stock instantly, and 'only 9 packets left' flags what's about to go. The rack and the packet page cohere as one shop.

1.rationale: The numbered list is clean but price and stock are set small at the foot of each entry, and season fit is text-only with no structural grouping, so glance speed depends on reading. The month filter is simple and predictable.

2.rationale: Money path is fully conventional: bold price, standard stock language, quantity plus 'Add to basket' immediately under the product title. 'Price pending — ask us' handles the null price without inventing a mechanic.

3.rationale: All four traps pass — red 'Out of stock', 'Price pending — ask us', '(estimated)' germination, and stock-true 'only 9 packets left' — but the UK-only shipping note is a single small centered line that is easy to skim past. It is at least present on both surfaces and repeated in the buy box.

4.rationale: Headings and body serif are comfortable, but the letterspaced small-caps metadata and small stock text run tiny for older readers at default zoom. Gates passed, yet perceived legibility is the weakest of the three.

5.rationale: Beautiful typographic discipline — consistent rules, numbering, measure, and a restrained paper palette that survives dark mode intact. The two surfaces read as pages of the same printed annual.

6.rationale: Sowing table, difficulty, potting-shed note, and both companions with price and stock are all present in a calm reading order below the buy box. Nothing needed for the decision is missing.

7.rationale: 'A page from the shop's printed seed annual' lands in one sentence and shows in every layer — numbered entries, 'No. 1 in the annual' on the product page, 'read slowly, choose well'. It borrows a form gardeners already trust rather than boutique gloss.

8.rationale: The only breaks visible are the two declared ones: the card-free annual list and the small-caps specimen labels. Entry mechanics and the product-page money path stay strictly conventional.

9.rationale: 'Two of us keep this list; every variety on it is one we grow ourselves. Read slowly, choose well' is unhurried and unpublishable by a competitor unchanged. 'Price pending — ask us' keeps the neighborly register inside a mechanic.

10.rationale: A return visitor must read down the whole list to find what's in stock or in season — stock marks are small and there's no seasonal structure, only the filter. The two surfaces do cohere tightly as one annual.

1.rationale: Grouping by sowing window plus per-entry month-band bars answers 'what suits my season' structurally, with bold prices and color-coded stock beneath. The plain month dropdown and window jump-links make filtering predictable.

2.rationale: Controls themselves are exactly conventional, but the product page runs title, then the full sowing table, and only then the price/buy box — burying the price below the calendar is the one clever placement in an otherwise clean money path. Catalog entries keep price and stock conventional.

3.rationale: All four traps pass, and honesty is actively reinforced — a marginal note explains the estimated germination figure and another admits the sweet pea 'takes an autumn sowing too' when its section says winter. Stock-derived claims match the sealed numbers.

4.rationale: Type sizes and targets are generous and nothing depends on hover; the tiny month-band squares are always backed by a bold 'Sow …' text line. Small italic marginalia is the only strain for older eyes.

5.rationale: The almanac system — rules, bands, margin column — is disciplined and holds on mobile by inlining the marginalia. The plum accent for links and the basket button sits slightly apart from the green system, and turns pink in dark mode.

6.rationale: Calendar-first with a month-band diagram, difficulty, 'From the margin' grower note, and both companions on one page — arguably the best fit to a first-time gardener's actual deciding question. Everything needed is present.

7.rationale: 'An almanac opened on the potting bench' is one sentence and structural — the visitor genuinely finds their month before their packet, and marginalia carries the growers' presence. It is service culture built into the information architecture, not gloss.

8.rationale: The two declared breaks (calendar-primary organization, almanac marginalia) are executed as declared, but the product page's buy-box-after-calendar ordering is an undeclared checkout-adjacent placement change, which scores as a mistake under the budget rule.

9.rationale: The marginalia is the knowledgeable neighbor verbatim — 'for the patient gardener', 'the widest window in the almanac — five months of it', 'takes an autumn sowing too'. No competitor could lift these notes unchanged.

10.rationale: A repeat visitor lands on their current window via the jump-links or filter and reads stock states in color immediately; the month bands make in-season checks near-instant. Almanac and packet page cohere as one shop.
